rationale_evidence.anchor: 95.6 — But classification alone is insufficient ... K=Internal. Actor is also Internal. That does not necessarily imply access. There may be Purpose, Domain, Role, NeedToKnow constraints.
rationale_evidence.statement: Argues matching classification alone (Internal knowledge, Internal actor) does not necessarily imply access; Purpose, Domain, Role, and NeedToKnow may also constrain it.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 95.21 — AI creates a new information-flow problem ... AccessControl(Input) is not sufficient. We also need OutputControl.
rationale_evidence.statement: Argues AI necessitates OutputControl in addition to input AccessControl, since output may leak information from restricted inputs.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 95.28 — Privacy and uncertainty ... Should the system reveal P(H)=0.9? Sensitivity can apply to raw facts, probabilities, models, correlations, predictions, conclusions.
rationale_evidence.statement: Argues sensitivity can apply not only to raw facts but to probabilities, models, correlations, predictions, and conclusions.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 95.30 — Privacy-preserving aggregation ... Count(Employees)=500 instead of individual records. But even aggregation can leak information if the group is too small.
rationale_evidence.statement: Notes aggregation (e.g. counts/averages) can safely obscure individuals, but small-group aggregation can still leak information.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 95.37 — Right to deletion versus provenance ... K must be deleted under an applicable policy. But another artifact contains Provenance(K). What exactly must be removed? We need explicit data-lifecycle semantics.
rationale_evidence.statement: Raises the tension between right-to-deletion and provenance-preservation: deleting K while another artifact retains Provenance(K) requires explicit data-lifecycle semantics.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 95.41 — Immutable audit logs ... Auditability may require ImmutableHistory. Privacy policy may require Deletion. These cannot always both be satisfied naively. KnowledgeOS must not hide the conflict.
rationale_evidence.statement: States the genuine tension between ImmutableHistory (auditability) and Deletion (privacy), which cannot always be naively both satisfied and must not be hidden.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 95.43 — Separation of identity and event semantics ... preserve EventID and EventSemantics while separately managing identifying attributes. This can reduce unnecessary exposure.
rationale_evidence.statement: Proposes separating EventID/EventSemantics from identifying attributes as an architectural technique to reduce unnecessary exposure while preserving audit needs.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 95.51 — Security before retrieval versus security after retrieval ... If we retrieve restricted information and only afterward filter it, the information has already entered the processing environment. Authorization should preferably constrain retrieval itself.
rationale_evidence.statement: States the key architectural principle that authorization should preferably constrain retrieval itself, since post-retrieval filtering still exposes restricted information to the processing environment.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 95.56 — Privacy and embeddings ... Embedding(K) cannot automatically be treated as non-sensitive merely because it is a vector.
rationale_evidence.statement: States embeddings may themselves encode sensitive information and cannot be treated as non-sensitive merely for being vectors.

## Rationale
Argues matching classification alone (Internal knowledge, Internal actor) does not necessarily imply access; Purpose, Domain, Role, and NeedToKnow may also constrain it. [S0994] Argues AI necessitates OutputControl in addition to input AccessControl, since output may leak information from restricted inputs. [S0994] Argues sensitivity can apply not only to raw facts but to probabilities, models, correlations, predictions, and conclusions. [S0994] Notes aggregation (e.g. counts/averages) can safely obscure individuals, but small-group aggregation can still leak information. [S0994] Raises the tension between right-to-deletion and provenance-preservation: deleting K while another artifact retains Provenance(K) requires explicit data-lifecycle semantics. [S0994] States the genuine tension between ImmutableHistory (auditability) and Deletion (privacy), which cannot always be naively both satisfied and must not be hidden. [S0994] Proposes separating EventID/EventSemantics from identifying attributes as an architectural technique to reduce unnecessary exposure while preserving audit needs. [S0994] States the key architectural principle that authorization should preferably constrain retrieval itself, since post-retrieval filtering still exposes restricted information to the processing environment. [S0994] States embeddings may themselves encode sensitive information and cannot be treated as non-sensitive merely for being vectors. [S0994]
